statement: Every protocol input state event receipt cursor and phase remains in its declared finite domain
Distinct caller task keys cannot map to one dense task identifier
Every active dense identifier has exactly one key and both mapping directions round-trip
Plan identity binds canonical keys dependencies effects costs budget task semantics and schema profile
Validated plan and checkpoint inputs are immutable throughout execution
Every journal event has the exact one-based ordinal and canonical plan identity
Journal event identifiers are unique within one plan
An open journal contains at most one event per task and a terminal journal at most one additional event
A terminal journal ends in exactly one typed terminal event
Durable journal contents are append-only and never rewritten
An accepted checkpoint is bound to the active structural plan identity
A stale plan identity is rejected before task effects
Corrupt shape cursor count or event identifiers are rejected before task effects
The zero-based next-task cursor equals the length of the committed success prefix
Invalid checkpoints and unsafe recovery publish no task effects or invented events
A canonical journal append durably precedes logical publication
Publishing the same plan-and-ordinal event identifier more than once is idempotent
Publication receipts form a canonical contiguous prefix of the journal
Every receipt references a durable event and recovery never invents an event
Every validated durable event is eventually published exactly once logically
Publication receipts are monotone across every transition
A crash preserves the authoritative journal and durable publication receipts
A pre-journal in-flight task without a deterministic idempotent or transactional witness fails closed
A deterministic replay-safe in-flight task may resume from the same immutable plan
Resuming any valid committed prefix reconstructs the uninterrupted canonical journal
Resumed observable results equal the serial uninterrupted reference
Physical worker completion order is normalized before durable observation
Failure incomplete cancellation resource limitation and success completion remain distinct terminal outcomes under deterministic cancellation-before-resource boundary priority
Completed means every task succeeded and a final completed event was durably published
Canonical plan event and checkpoint codecs reject every append exceeding declared byte or item limits
Validation publication and replay perform linear bounded work in keys tasks events and bytes
Auxiliary durable-machine state is linear and all input-shaped state is heap resident
Native call-stack depth is constant with respect to tasks dependencies journal events and encoded bytes
Each replay step strictly decreases a bounded remaining-event measure
Every fair validated finite protocol run reaches one typed terminal state
